label: Bool Sum Counts True
description: Because booleans are integers in Python, summing booleans counts how many values are `True`.

label: String Immutable Reassign
description: String methods return a new string; the original string stays unchanged unless you reassign it.

label: Implicit Return None
description: A function without an explicit `return` returns `None`.

label: Method Returns None
description: A mutating method changed the object in place, but the expression itself evaluates to `None`.

label: Comparison Chain
description: Chained comparisons like `a < b < c` are not the same as comparing booleans or tuples.

label: Default Arg Optional
description: A parameter with a default is optional when calling the function.

label: Float Int String Equality
description: Python can treat some numeric types as equal (`True == 1`, `1 == 1.0`), but strings stay separate.

label: Enumerate Gives Index Value
description: `enumerate(iterable)` yields `(index, value)` pairs, in that order.

label: Local Scope Nameerror
description: A local name is not visible outside the function where it was created.

label: Zip Pairs Positionally
description: `zip(a, b)` pairs items by position, not by value matching.

label: Date Directive Order
description: Datetime directives must match the input order exactly (`%d/%m/%Y` is not `%m/%d/%Y`).

label: Join Called On Separator
description: `join` is called on the separator string, not on the list of pieces.

label: Loc Vs Iloc
description: `loc` uses labels; `iloc` uses integer positions.

label: Strptime Vs Strftime
description: `strptime` parses strings into datetime objects; `strftime` formats datetime objects into strings.

label: Builtin Return Type
description: The code fails because the built-in returns a different type than the distractor assumes.

label: Dict Counting Pattern
description: The pattern should accumulate counts into a dictionary instead of overwriting or appending elsewhere.

label: Keys Vs Values
description: The question distinguishes between dictionary keys and dictionary values; distractors swap them.

label: Missing Self
description: Instance methods need `self` as the first parameter in the method definition.

label: Sort Vs Sorted
description: `sorted(x)` returns a new sorted object; `x.sort()` mutates in place and returns `None`.

label: Timedelta Requires Datetime
description: Date arithmetic with `timedelta` works on date/datetime objects, not raw strings.

label: Attribute Not On Self
description: Instance state should be stored on `self`, not as a bare local variable that disappears after `__init__`.

label: Dict Comp Key Value Order
description: Dictionary comprehension syntax is `{key_expr: value_expr for ...}` in that order.

label: Return In Init
description: `__init__` initializes the object and should not return a normal value.

label: Dict Iterates Keys
description: Looping directly over a dictionary yields keys.

label: Dict Order Not Equality
description: Dictionary equality depends on matching key-value pairs, not insertion order.

label: Negative Step Direction
description: With a negative step, the slice must move from right to left; otherwise it can be empty.

label: Slice Stop Exclusive
description: A slice includes the start index but excludes the stop index.

label: Custom Index Not Zero Based
description: A custom DataFrame index means label-based selection is not the same as row position.

label: Args Tuple Shape
description: `*args` collects extra positional arguments into a tuple.

label: Assignment Makes Local
description: Assigning to a name inside a function makes it local unless you declare otherwise.

label: Both Neither All Logic
description: Evaluate each statement separately before touching “both”, “neither”, or “all of the above”.

label: Broadcast Shape Mismatch
description: The operation tries to combine objects whose shapes do not align for broadcasting.

label: Compare Both Directions
description: Comparison-style methods often need to consider both directions or both objects symmetrically.

label: Comprehension If Else Position
description: The inline `x if cond else y` belongs before the `for`; a filter-only `if` goes after the `for`.

label: Datetime Arg Order
description: When building a `datetime`, the positional order is year, month, day (then time parts).

label: Format Placeholder Mismatch
description: The formatting expression has the wrong placeholder names or positions.

label: Inclusive Plus One
description: Inclusive end-points in loop/range questions often require a `+ 1`.

label: Keyword Binding By Name
description: Keyword arguments bind by parameter name, not by position.

label: Kwargs Values Not Keys
description: `**kwargs` stores keyword arguments in a dictionary of key-value pairs.

label: Map Element Only Vs Apply Row
description: `map` works element-wise on a Series; row-wise logic across multiple columns usually needs `apply(axis=1)` or vectorized code.

label: Map Expression Not Function
description: `map`/`apply` need a function or callable, not a value that was already computed.

label: Membership Checks Keys
description: `in` on a dictionary checks keys by default, not values.

label: Method Call In Fstring
description: In f-strings, you still need valid Python expressions; missing parentheses or quotes break them.

label: Misspelled Variable Name
description: The code references a different variable name than the one that was actually defined.

label: Mutable Default List
description: Using a mutable object like `[]` as a default can leak state across calls.

label: Series Vs Dataframe Shape
description: Single-bracket vs double-bracket selection changes whether you get a Series or a DataFrame.

label: State Stored On Instance
description: If later methods need the value, store it on the instance as an attribute.

label: Vectorized Ops Vs Map
description: Many column operations can be done directly with vectorized arithmetic/string methods instead of element-wise mapping.

label: Append Index Vs Value
description: Appending to a list adds a value; it does not create or shift indices the way distractors imply.

label: Lexicographic Vs Sum
description: `max()` on lists compares lexicographically unless you tell it to compare by a derived numeric key.

label: Replace Count Order
description: The optional count in `replace` comes after old and new strings.

label: Shuffle Sort In Place
description: `list.sort()` and `random.shuffle()` mutate a list in place instead of returning a sorted/shuffled copy.

label: String Not Datetime
description: String methods and datetime methods are not interchangeable; convert first if needed.

label: Boolean Mask Parentheses
description: Compound pandas boolean masks need parentheses around each comparison.

label: Case Method Pipeline
description: Case-changing methods return new strings, so multi-step pipelines must use the returned value.

label: Condition Precedence Brackets
description: Boolean expressions become error-prone when `and`/`or` precedence is not made explicit.

label: Count Is Method
description: `count` is a method on the sequence/string object, not a standalone built-in here.

label: Find Minus One Index Valueerror
description: `find` returns `-1` when missing; `index` raises an error.

label: Invalid Dataframe Tuple Index
description: A plain DataFrame cannot be indexed with a tuple the way the distractor attempts.

label: Lambda Call Shape
description: The lambda or higher-order function expects a function object, not the result of calling it too early.

label: Parse Host Before Extension
description: When parsing URLs/emails, isolate the host/domain before trying to take the extension/TLD.

label: Range Stop Exclusive
description: `range(start, stop)` stops before `stop`.

label: While Condition Off By One
description: The loop condition is off by one, so it runs one time too many or too few.

label: Format Too Early
description: Formatting happened before the needed values were available or before iteration finished.

label: Self Passed Twice
description: When you call `obj.method(...)`, Python passes `self` automatically; do not pass it again.

label: Sort Index Vs Sort Values
description: `sort_index()` reorders by labels; `sort_values()` reorders by data values.

label: Column Transform Assignment
description: Creating or updating a column requires assigning the transformed Series back to the DataFrame.

label: Negative Indices
description: Negative indices count from the end of the sequence.

label: Nested Index Order
description: Nested indexing must be applied in the correct order: outer container first, then inner item.

label: Sorted Running Total Shape
description: The distractor produces the wrong shape or nesting when trying to sort or accumulate running totals.

label: Zip Next Link
description: Creating “next item” dictionaries usually needs `zip(items, items[1:])` or a similar offset pairing.

label: Dataframe Column Lists Same Length
description: When constructing a DataFrame from lists, the columns must have matching lengths.

label: Import Alias Name Mismatch
description: When you import with an alias, only the alias is available in that scope.

label: Overlap Is Not Nonoverlap
description: Overlap conditions are easiest to write by negating the non-overlap cases carefully.

label: Set Removes Duplicates
description: A set removes duplicates and does not preserve list-style ordering semantics.
